chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, altogether, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Durust, from Zayd al-Shahham, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Therefore avoid the uncleanness of the idols and avoid false words.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The uncleanness of the idols' is chess, and 'false words' is singing.
ai.seo_question: What does the Imam say is the meaning of 'uncleanness of idols' and 'false words' in Surah Al-Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Zayd al-Shahham queries Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the interpretation of Surah Al-Hajj (22:30), where the Imam identifies 'uncleanness of idols' specifically as chess (*al-shatranj*) and 'false words' as singing (*al-ghina'*). This narration is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for establishing the prohibition of chess, linking it to the spiritual impurity of idols, while also categorizing musical entertainment as a form of falsehood that distracts from divine remembrance.
